headline: PSX slips as US-Iran deal hopes fade, but the domestic story -- cooling inflation, rising reserves, rich T-bill yields -- still tilts the desk toward banks.
summary: PSX fell 0.81% on 2026-08-11 (KSE-100 to 179,846.68) as investors pared back hopes for a US-Iran deal -- a reminder that Middle-East headline risk can still move the tape even though the desk's broader risk gauge reads 'calm.' Underneath the daily noise, the domestic story stays supportive: July CPI eased to 9.2%, SBP is holding at 11.5% into the September 14 meeting, and reserves rose for a second straight week to $17.04bn. T-bill and PIB yields (11.70%-12.30%) still sit comfortably above the policy rate, keeping the carry trade in banks attractive. The desk stays selective -- leaning into banks and pausing on energy-import-sensitive names.

sectors.name: Banks
sectors.why: T-bill (11.70%) and PIB (12.30%) yields sit well above the 11.5% policy rate and CPI cooling to 9.2% keeps the SBP hold intact into the Sept 14 MPC -- a clean carry story, and most bank names screen 'attractive' on cheap P/E and covered dividends.

sectors.name: OMCs & Refineries
sectors.why: Brent is up 5.7% over the past month and gold's continued safe-haven bid signal lingering global stress, both of which squeeze margins under PSX's daily fuel-price revision regime.

sectors.name: E&P (OGDC/PPL/MARI)
sectors.why: Higher oil is a tailwind for upstream earnings, but the fundamental read on the big three is 'mixed,' so the desk isn't chasing the group just because energy prices are firm.

sectors.name: Textiles / Exporters
sectors.why: FY26 closed with a fragile current account ($139mn deficit) and no fresher export data has come in to change that picture, so exporter margins stay a soft spot.

watchlist.angle: A volume-leads-price signal (obv_divergence_up) is live today with a strong record on BML's own history -- 97% hit rate over 89 trades, still 83% out-of-sample -- and fundamentals back it up: 'attractive' rating, cheap P/E, 32% net margin. Results are due 2026-08-28.
watchlist.risk: The 97% win rate is worked out from BML's own trading history over 89 trades, not a market-wide law -- one earnings surprise could dent it. The stock also pays no dividend, so the return case is pure price.

watchlist.angle: A 50-day-high breakout is triggering now (58% hit rate over 26 trades, still 60% out-of-sample), and momentum backs it up -- RSI near 68, price above both its 20- and 50-day averages, volume running 2.25x normal. Fundamentals are 'mixed' but cheap (P/E 5.27, forward P/E 4.73 pointing to earnings growth). Results aren't due until late September.
watchlist.risk: Small-cap (35B market cap, beta 1.04) -- moves fast both ways, and the breakout's 26-trade sample is thinner than BML's, so the edge is less proven.

watchlist.angle: The desk's sma_golden_cross backtest on BAFL has a strong record (75% hit rate, +4.67% net expectancy, 100% out-of-sample), fundamentals are 'attractive' (P/E 5.57, 10.03% dividend yield), and a confirmed Rs3.0/share dividend book-closure lands 2026-08-13.
watchlist.risk: The golden-cross signal isn't firing today -- this is a proven historical strategy on the name, not a live trigger, so entry timing is less certain.

watchlist.angle: The reclaim_sma200 strategy on AKBL has a positive track record (56% hit rate, +1.47% net expectancy, 80% out-of-sample), fundamentals are 'attractive' (P/E 6.07, 4.66% yield), and a confirmed Rs2.0/share dividend book-closure lands 2026-08-13.
watchlist.risk: Same sector and same catalyst week as BAFL -- the two aren't a diversified pair, and the strategy's edge here is smaller than BAFL's.

catalysts.event: Dividend book closures: AKBL (Rs2.0/share) and BAFL (Rs3.0/share)
Next SBP T-bill auction and weekly FX reserves print

risks: Middle-East diplomacy risk cuts both ways -- today's 0.81% slide was driven by fading hopes for a US-Iran deal, and the desk's georisk gauge still carries elevated gold (74/100) and energy (63/100) stress scores even though the headline composite reads 'calm' (37/100).

The PIB curve steepened at the last auction (10Y cutoff up to 12.30%, 15Y to 12.49%, with the 2Y rejected outright) -- the market is pricing a hold-for-longer SBP, which caps upside for anything leaning on an early rate cut.
Two of today's watchlist names (BAFL, AKBL) are both banks with dividend catalysts landing the same week -- a reminder that ex-dividend price adjustments are not the same thing as a trading edge.
disclaimer: Research, not advice. The desk generates signals; it does not place orders. Losses are expected.
